claims.text: The initial target MPEA is a single-phase BCC or FCC solid solution with room-temperature tensile ductility below 5%.
SCCP can overcome the room-temperature strength-ductility trade-off in the target MPEA family.
Solution treatment followed by quenching creates a supersaturated solid solution.
Subsequent low-temperature aging nucleates and grows coherent nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates.
The coherent secondary phase may be B2 or L12 depending on alloy composition.
The desired coherent precipitate size is 5-20 nm.
High precipitate-matrix coherency promotes dislocation transmission rather than deformation solely by Orowan looping.
An appropriate SCCP schedule is solution annealing at 1100-1300°C for 1-2 hours, rapid quenching, and aging at 400-700°C for 10-100 hours.
An argon atmosphere prevents oxidation during the high-temperature treatments.
Coherent precipitate-matrix interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Dislocation transmission at coherent interfaces relieves stress concentrations that would otherwise promote premature crack initiation.
Incoherent precipitates cause dislocation pile-up and void nucleation.
Coherent precipitates preserve ductility while also providing precipitation strengthening.
The treated target alloy will achieve room-temperature yield strength above 1.0 GPa and tensile elongation above 10%.
The treated target alloy will achieve room-temperature ultimate tensile strength above 2.0 GPa.
The alloy will retain more than 80% of its room-temperature mechanical properties at 800°C.
The resulting microstructure will contain a uniform distribution of coherent nanoscale precipitates rather than coarse incoherent precipitates or lamellae.
Standard annealing or uncontrolled aging generally produces either coarse incoherent precipitates and embrittlement or no precipitation and low strength.
The strategy is most effective when the alloy can form coherent precipitates with lattice mismatch below 5%.
Higher-temperature or longer-time standard aging can be used to produce an incoherent-precipitate control condition.
